implementation_observed: Uses music21 Note/Chord recursion; excludes print-hidden, slash-head, unpitched and chord symbols; struck excludes grace and tie continuations.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Appropriate library-first shared policy; no duplicate MusicXML note parser for the ordinary path. Custom filtering is legitimately product-specific.
correctness_and_musical_risks: A global 'printed note' rule is a useful default, but printed cues may be unplayed and notation may encode hidden performance notes relevant to actual sound; explicitly label the count visual/printed, not all heard notes. _keep on chord member receives member notehead/style; reasonable. Chord-level duration.isGrace potentially differs among members. Some feature files bypass _notes, so 'every row' is overstated.
test_quality_and_unverified: Top comment reports examples and corpus counts; not independently rerun; check cue vs actual performance case, slash-head in chord, mixed hidden/visible chord, ties and grace.
recommended_correction: Document visual-note versus performance-note semantics; verify edge cases and consistency in raw-XML rows. Do not rewrite the shared filter.
code_evidence: _keep(); printed(); struck(); _notes.py lines ~19-50
claude_ruling: PARTLY. Agree to label the rule as PRINTED notes (what a reader sees), not heard notes; the docstring says printed. Disagree that printed cue-size notes may be unplayed in OUR files: the visible ones read (Chopin Op. 25/1, K. 467 arrangement) are played. 'Every row uses it' was overstated: E11/E40/E12 rhythm rows filter hidden notes themselves. NO CHANGE to the rule; E40 now uses _keep (below).

implementation_observed: ElementTree raw MXL/XML loader, raw bar labels, measure time-cursor calculation, generic spanner pairing, and direction cursor; functions shared by multiple row modules.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Measured gaps in music21 justify narrow raw reads, but this module is already a generic low-level MusicXML state engine. Its edge semantics should be validated before using it as authority across E04/E21/E23/E24/E25.
correctness_and_musical_risks: directions() computes offset by int(float(duration/offset)) and tracks a single divisions value; noninteger offset and edge precision can be lost; floating division before int is not exact. raw_root handles compressed score-partwise only, silently strips namespaces (loses namespace distinctions). pair_spans FIFO with same-time reorder is a heuristic, not universally correct for overlapping same-number spanners. bar_label caches by path and object id, with no cache invalidation; _NUMBERS uses first part's bar IDs even for other parts.
test_quality_and_unverified: Shared helpers need adversarial MXL rootfile, subdivisions/offsets, same-time line events and ambiguous multivoice spanners; measured corpus assertion is insufficient proof of general pairing semantics.
recommended_correction: Use Fraction from integer XML values rather than int(float(...)); narrow each gap read and mark ambiguous paired spans UNKNOWN; use per-part bar numbering when parts differ; exercise shared helper tests separately.
code_evidence: raw_root(), bar_label(), bar_lengths(), pair_spans(), directions(); int(float(...)) in directions
claude_ruling: AGREE on the main point. FIXED: directions() now uses exact Fractions (no int(float())). FIXED, and worse than ChatGPT saw: bar_label never reached the file at all (getContextByClass(Score) returns None), so every label had fallen back to music21's number+suffix; it now finds the score through the part's sites, with a new test. pair_spans: kept, measured (ottava identical either way; hairpins 5 unclosed vs 27); ambiguous pairs as UNKNOWN is LATER. First-part bar numbers: E32 measured 0 files whose parts differ in measure count; NO CHANGE.

reports: Number of parts, part names and instruments, staves per part; layout verdict: SUPPORTED (one pitched part with two staves) or UNSUPPORTED with the reason.
definition: Parts from <part-list>/<score-part>; staves from <attributes><staves>. Only one pitched part with two staves is supported; staff 1 and staff 2 are then the two staves. Every other layout (two parts, one staff, a voice or other instrument part, staves changing mid-piece) is UNSUPPORTED and every per-staff row below returns UNKNOWN for that file instead of guessing.
implementation: Raw MusicXML walk with ElementTree, namespace-agnostic, opening .mxl through META-INF/container.xml (as build_available.py and export_shortlist.py already do). music21 score.parts (two PartStaff objects) as the second reader. Reuse quality_check.not_piano for instrument names.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: the validators' own raw walk read all 2,020 notated files with 0 errors. music21 gives two PartStaff for a two-staff part; partitura gives one Part with number_of_staves 2 (new-library-research A).
pitfalls: Two parts both named Piano (a right-hand/left-hand split or a duet: several in the 109-file shortlist); voice plus piano (shortlist Ave Maria, part 'Voix'); unnamed parts; a staff added mid-piece.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a standard grand-staff file -> SUPPORTED. Fail: a voice-plus-piano file -> UNSUPPORTED (extra part). Fool: two parts, each one staff, both named 'Piano' -> UNSUPPORTED, not merged by guess.
in_our_files: <staff> element present in 714 of 842 (84.8%), a proxy for one part with two staves
used_for: Every row below (precondition); step 4: checking that a generated exercise has the intended layout
why_easy: Direct element read; the only decision is to refuse unusual layouts rather than interpret them.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Reading the encoded part/staff layout is easy; *supporting only* one pitched two-staff part is a product restriction, not evidence other arrangements cannot be analysed. Many useful beginner one-staff pieces, solo-piano reductions encoded in two parts, lead sheets and duets would become UNKNOWN. Keep raw layout inventory for every file; support canonical two-staff scores first, but return UNSUPPORTED only for analyses that truly require that layout. Music21 PartStaff is not guaranteed to appear as two Score.parts for every score. Show supported-corpus coverage and losses before accepting this boundary.
implementation_observed: Groups music21 PartStaff / Part, aggregates pitched staves and attempts two-piano-stave selection using quality_check.not_piano.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Strong reuse of music21's staff split, preferable to bespoke part XML walking; old research benchmark is asserted, not reproduced in this review.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Source-part grouping uses splitting '-Staff' suffix plus adjacency; legitimate source part IDs ending in '-Staff...' or reordered staff groups can be grouped wrongly. Any part with at least one pitched note makes all its staves 'pitched' in keep, including empty/only-rest staff; contradicts 'pitched staves' semantics but may be intentional layout preservation. Piano-vs-other-instrument check depends on names and imported quality_check heuristic; unlabeled non-piano parts can be accepted as piano. Instrument and staff are not hand.
test_quality_and_unverified: Requires 1-staff pieces, two Parts not two PartStaffs, three-staff layouts, empty staff, part-order interleave and ambiguous instrument naming tests; no independent full-corpus check.
recommended_correction: Keep music21 primary; preserve explicit source-part identifiers more robustly, distinguish layout staves from note-bearing staves, and label two_piano_staves provisional from metadata not verified piano identity.
code_evidence: layout(); source=p.id.rsplit('-Staff',1)[0]; parts[-1]['pitched']; keep; not_piano
claude_ruling: PARTLY. '-Staff' is music21's own PartStaff id scheme, not a user id, so the split is safe for files music21 parsed. two_piano_staves rests on part names (not verified piano identity): agreed, it is a name check and says so via two_staff_reason. NO CHANGE.

reports: For each measure: position index, printed number (measure@number), implicit flag, notated length against the time signature (full, short, over-full).
definition: Notated length of a measure = the largest end time over its voices, from <duration>, <backup> and <forward> in divisions; compared with the time signature in force.
implementation: Raw walk (the same logic file_checks.py already uses for its bar check). music21 Measure.number and paddingLeft as the second reader. All later rows report locations with the printed number, so a reader or a Haiku agent can find the bar in the score.
library_and_prior_evidence: file_checks.py already flags under-full and over-full interior bars on this pipeline; the old project's raw walk did the same.
pitfalls: Printed numbers repeated or with suffixes ('12a'), multi-bar rests, first and second endings sharing numbers, cue-size notes counted into the length.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 4/4 bar of four quarters -> full. Fail: 4/4 bar with three quarters and no rest -> short. Fool: a bar whose second voice has a <forward> instead of rests -> full (largest voice end), not short.
used_for: Locations in every row; anacrusis (E10); excerpts handed to Haiku agents; step 4 generator output check
why_easy: Arithmetic over durations already implemented and tested in file_checks.py.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Keep both stable measure index and printed number (including suffixes) because repeated numbers/first and second endings are not unique. Time cursors must be tracked separately for backup/forward and voices with changed divisions; maximum end time is *elapsed encoded extent*, not proof of a metrically complete, well-rested bar. Report explicit rests versus unfilled voice gaps separately; distinguish pickup, final short measure, cadenza and corrupted bars. Good reusable foundation, but the stated forward-only fool test cannot certify editorial completeness.
implementation_observed: music21 measure lengths and time signatures; raw implicit flag and targeted fallback raw time cursor for full-measure-rest cases; reports bar ID, encoded extent, nominal, gaps.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Good choice of music21 and narrow XML fallback; explicit correction provenance is helpful.
correctness_and_musical_risks: The >1/8-quarter correction cutoff is ad hoc and silently keeps smaller real disagreements; short/overfull classification can be distorted by notationally legitimate pickup and ending bars. Gap computation uses each voice's maximum note/rest end, potentially flags legitimate pickups and trailing voices without meaning an error; global index alignment across staves assumes matching measure order; printed number obtained from first part.
test_quality_and_unverified: Need unequal measure count/index, fractional tuplets, full-measure rests in pickups, interleaved voices, no time signature and mismatched parts; score was not executed here.
recommended_correction: Expose both music21 and raw extent whenever they disagree rather than using an unsupported 1/8 threshold; use explicit uncertainty/flags for legitimate incomplete voices and index mismatch; retain unique measure index plus printed label.
code_evidence: bars(); if abs(written[i]-length)>Fraction(1,8); gaps end<nominal
claude_ruling: PARTLY. The 1/8-quarter cutoff is measured, not ad hoc: integer-duration drift is at most 0.03 quarter (16 bars, music21 right) and real stretched rests differ by 1/2 or more (30 bars). corrected_from already exposes music21's value whenever the cursor wins. Gaps are reported as observations, not errors. NO CHANGE.

fact: Clefs and clef changes, per staff
reports: Starting clef of each staff (sign, line, octave change); every change as (bar, staff, from, to, inside the bar or at its start); count of changes per staff.
definition: A change is a <clef number=staff> whose sign, line or octave change differs from the clef in force on that staff. A clef equal to the one in force (restated at a system break) is not a change.
implementation: Raw walk of <attributes><clef> including attributes in the middle of a measure; a clef without a number attribute applies to staff 1. music21 clef.Clef objects per PartStaff as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: raw walk validated (clef changes in 145 PDMX ids, 96 inside a bar; same-clef restatements in 50 files not counted). The old app detector read staff 2 as bass and never read the clef, which failed on clef changes. music21 ran on corpus scores: staff 2 of Clara Schumann Op. 1 No. 1 has 14 bass, 7 treble and 1 treble-8va clef objects.
pitfalls: Restated clefs; cue clefs; treble-8va or bass-8vb clefs (octave change); a staff that starts in the 'wrong' clef (both staves treble).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: corpus Maple Leaf Rag -> clef changes on staff 2 at bars 9 and 13 (as music21 reads it). Fail: a file with only the opening clefs -> 0. Fool: the same treble clef restated at every system -> 0 changes.
in_our_files: 348 of 842 files have more than two <clef> elements (includes restatements, so an upper bound)
used_for: A.1 (both clefs), 6.7 (clef changes in reading), E05 ledger lines (needs the clef in force), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; the only rule is 'changed from the clef in force'.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Compare sign, line and clef-octave-change at actual in-measure position; preserve the staff clef state from prior measures. No-number means the score-part default, usually staff 1, but check multi-clef attributes; track initial clefs separately from changes. Test same-clef restatement, one-staff two-hand display, mid-bar change and 8va clefs. E01 already filters many layouts, so do not conflate these with hand ownership.
implementation_observed: Iterates music21 clef elements per pitched staff, compares sign/line/octave; captures first clef and genuine changes with location.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Correct library-first approach, no evident duplicate parser.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Potential missing opening clef if parser inserts implicit clefs; preserving actual clef at each note for dependent calculations more important than counting. Repeated signature at same location deduplicated, intentional. Missing staff clef gives no start entry, so per_staff totals omit staff silently; clef sequence relies on music21 recursion order, especially midbar multi-voice.
test_quality_and_unverified: Claimed 833-file agreement from header, not independently reproduced; adversarial clef-change-midbar, cue, instrument swap and nonstandard clef tests.
recommended_correction: Retain; add missing-clef UNKNOWN and validate one in-measure change against XML/engraving when integrated.
code_evidence: clefs(); m.clef.Clef, sig=(sign,line,octaveChange), prev
claude_ruling: AGREE. FIXED: a staff with no clef now reports start UNKNOWN instead of being missing.

reports: Each span: staff, kind and size, first and last bar, notes inside; spans not closed are listed as UNCLOSED with their start.
definition: <octave-shift type='up|down|stop' size='8|15' number='n'> pairs, matched by number within a staff. Notes inside a span are those between start and stop in that staff.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 spanner.Ottava as the second reader. In our files music21 imports the notes under an ottava at sounding pitch (Ottava.transposing is False); our probe on 4 candidate files found the same number of spans as the raw <octave-shift> starts in all 4.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: own span reading agreed with music21 on 81 of 93 files (exclusive stop); unclosed spans (3 in Malagueña), empty spans and '8va cont.' words occur. Never compared with a printed page.
pitfalls: Unclosed or empty spans; '8va' written only as <words> (no span); whether the stop note is inside the span (exclusive vs inclusive).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: an 8va over bars 5-6 of staff 1 -> one span, bars 5-6. Fail: no <octave-shift> -> none. Fool: '8va' typed as <words> with no <octave-shift> -> no span; listed under 'ottava words' only.
used_for: A.1 (a passage marked 8va), 7.8 (8va in reading), E05 (written position under an 8va)
why_easy: Direct read; library and raw reader agreed on our sample.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The MusicXML octave-shift type is from *printed* pitch to sounding pitch: a conventional 8va is a `down` shift in the element. Do not interpret `up` as sounding-up. `number` also scopes paired spanners; include `continue`, `<offset>`, and stop boundary ordering, preserving unclosed spans as UNKNOWN. Report encoded pitch and displayed pitch separately. Four sample matches support parsing, not direction/edge correctness. This is a high-impact prerequisite for E05 and E33.
implementation_observed: Uses raw octave-shift directions of type up/down/stop, intentionally skipping type=continue (formatting continuation), pairs starts with stops via shared FIFO helper, and counts music21 note onsets in completed spans; unclosed starts are reported.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Custom pairing has a concrete documented music21 10.5 failure rationale (lost within-bar/unclosed/mispaired spans), so this is justified in principle rather than automatically anti-library.
correctness_and_musical_risks: CORRECTION TO INITIAL REVIEW: type=continue is FILTERED OUT, NOT misclassified as a new start. MusicXML defines it as an intermediate formatting continuation; ignoring it does not by itself invalidate a correctly paired start-to-stop span. Isolated continuation marks lacking an opening start are unreported; overlapping same-number spans use a FIFO heuristic; the start<=onset<stop boundary and labels from first staff need checking when actual notation differs. Unclosed extents make dependent ledger counts uncertain.
test_quality_and_unverified: Static review only; E04 tests start/stop and unclosed, not type=continue; official MusicXML specification defines continue as intermediate, so ignoring it is potentially correct for complete spans. No independent printed bar comparison or runtime execution.
recommended_correction: Do not write a full continuation parser without a demonstrated incorrect result. Test start/continue/stop as ONE span and look for orphan continuations only if present in repertoire; check a disputed note at the stop boundary against printed notation, and explicitly propagate incomplete-ottava uncertainty where applicable.
code_evidence: events accepts el.get('type') in ('up','down','stop'); comment asserts continue handled but actually ignored; pair_spans start=e[4]!='stop'
claude_ruling: AGREE with the corrected review: type=continue is an intermediate mark and ignoring it is right for complete spans. FIXED: added the start/continue/stop test (one span, 6 notes). Stop-boundary check against print: LATER (plan: printed spot-checks).

reports: Per staff: notes by number of ledger lines needed (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, more than 5), above and below; the bars of notes with 1-2 and 3+ ledger lines.
definition: Written staff position from the clef in force and the written pitch (sounding pitch moved back by any ottava in force, E04). Ledger lines needed = how many lines beyond the five staff lines the note sits on or past: middle C in treble = 1 below; A5 in treble = 1 above; C6 in treble = 2 above; middle C in bass = 1 above; E2 in bass = 1 below.
implementation: music21: diatonicNoteNum of the written pitch against clef.lowestLine (treble 31, bass 19): below = (lowestLine - d) // 2 when d < lowestLine, above = (d - topLine) // 2 when d > topLine, with topLine = lowestLine + 8 (checked by hand: treble D4 0, C4 1, B3 1, A3 2; G5 0, A5 1, B5 1, C6 2; bass E2 1, C4 1). Each note of a chord counted; grace notes counted separately. Replaces rung_pieces.py's pitch-range proxy for B.1 and 1.1.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: own staff-position geometry validated on named pieces (Satie, Silent Night, We Three Kings); 6 or more ledger lines happen in 97 real files, many where an 8va mark was lost in transcription. The research agent checked a 3-line formula on 4 hand cases (C4 treble 1, A5 treble 1, C4 bass 1, E2 bass 1).
pitfalls: A lost 8va gives absurd counts: more than 5 is reported as 'possible missing 8va', not as a reading demand; cross-staff notes use the clef of the staff they are written on; the off-by-one between notes on a ledger line and in the space beyond it (the formula's main risk).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C4 treble 1 below; B3 treble 1 below (space under the first ledger line); D4 treble 0; A5 treble 1 above; B5 treble 1 above; C6 treble 2; E2 bass 1 below; C4 bass 1 above. Fail: notes inside the staff -> 0. Fool: written D6 under an 8va (sounding D7) -> 2 ledger lines, not 5.
used_for: B.1 (to two ledger lines), 1.1 (ledger lines above and below), reading difficulty, step 4 generator check (no note beyond the ledger lines a level allows)
why_easy: Small formula from two library values; the hand-made cases above pin every boundary.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Validate diatonic ledger-line arithmetic under both clefs and actual octave-shifts. Critical distinction: spaces beyond the staff count the number of ledger lines *passed*, not automatically one more (their examples look correct but require signed off-by-one cases). Treat high ledger counts as data, with a separate possible-8va warning rather than hiding valid difficult notes. Base on displayed note spelling and active clef, never MIDI-only spelling; staff number is not hand.
implementation_observed: Derives written staff position using music21 pitch spelling and clef sign/line/octaveChange, plus E04 raw 8va-derived shift; counts signed ledger lines.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Existing music21 pitch/clef used, custom small arithmetic justified. Raw E04 dependency is narrower than re-parsing notes.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Critical dependency on E04 pairing and ottava onset/stop. 'Unclosed' flag leaves affected written-pitch interpretation unknown, but still publishes ledger counts as though complete. Formula gives zero for the adjacent outside space and one for first ledger line, appropriate. Choice of n.getContextByClass(Clef) under intra-measure changes needs verification; clef octave behavior can be double-processed if music21 pitch semantics differ by importer.
test_quality_and_unverified: 4 hand examples claimed in header; cross-check 8va and 15ma, clef octave, notes precisely at boundaries, unclosed span and missing clef.
recommended_correction: Flag affected ranges/ledger totals partial-UNKNOWN when unclosed ottava or missing clef; validate printed coordinate against actual rendered score; first resolve E04.
code_evidence: ledger(); mine from ottava.spans; shift=next(...,0); unclosed_ottava flag alongside counts
claude_ruling: PARTLY. unclosed_ottava already flags the staff whose counts are partial; making the counts themselves UNKNOWN would hide the 939 good spans' files too. Clef context with mid-bar changes was probed (music21 finds the clef in force). NO CHANGE; printed check LATER.

reports: Fifths (and mode when written) at the start and at each change, with bar and staff; number of changes.
definition: <key><fifths> (and <mode>) per staff (number attribute) or for all staves; a change is a value different from the one in force. Non-traditional keys (<key-step>/<key-alter>) are reported as such.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 key.KeySignature as the second reader (some files give the subclass key.Key, so test with isinstance).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (Beethoven Symphony 7 four changes; key changes in 55 PDMX ids). The old app detector kept only the first key. music21 on corpus Maple Leaf Rag: -4, -5, -4 at bars 0, 51, 68.
pitfalls: Signatures restated at system breaks; cancellation naturals; per-staff keys; the written mode is often missing, so the mode is never inferred here.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: Maple Leaf Rag -> -4 (bar 0), -5 (bar 51), -4 (bar 68). Fail: a C major file with one signature -> one entry, 0 changes. Fool: G major restated at every system -> 0 changes.
used_for: B.4, 1.12 and the scale rungs' keys (which keys a piece is in), level fit (key signature size), step 4 generator check (requested key = written key)
why_easy: Direct read; library agreed on the corpus test.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Raw fifths and mode/key-step/alter plus location are explicit. Do not collapse nontraditional signatures to zero or infer the sounding tonic from them. Verify the `number` attribute for per-staff key and application at in-measure changes, mode absent, cancellation/naturals, and opening written key only. A printed key signature is a reading demand, not proof any changed degree occurs (E08 covers that).
implementation_observed: Reads music21 KeySignature per staff; compares actual written key changes; merges matching changes across staves.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Good direct music21 reuse with specialized duplicate-merge calculation.
correctness_and_musical_risks: The merged count keys include str(dict) instead of stable key-signature identifier; simultaneous different changes on different staves counted separately (could be desired); nontraditional altered pitches represented only as p.name, losing detailed order and cancellation. Missing opening key stored as no entry, not explicitly C/unknown; detect actual absence separately. Context may insert implicit C signature.
test_quality_and_unverified: Asserted 832/833 agreement not independently validated; test per-staff midbar, nontraditional/cancellation, courtesy restatement, missing mode.
recommended_correction: Keep library route; preserve structured nontraditional pitches and explicit absent signatures; confirm merge semantics for independent staff keys.
code_evidence: keys(); desc(); m.key.KeySignature; merged={(bar_index,offset,str(to))}
claude_ruling: PARTLY. str(dict) as a dedup key is stable for these values; probed: music21 does not insert an implicit C signature when none is written. NO CHANGE.

fact: Accidentals as encoded in the file
reports: Per staff: count of <accidental> elements by kind (sharp, flat, natural, double sharp, double flat), how many are cautionary or editorial; accidentals per 100 notes; bars with the most.
definition: Only the file's own <accidental> elements: what the file says is printed. Whether a given renderer would draw an accidental is NOT computed (that is the hard part; see pitfalls).
implementation: Raw walk of <note><accidental> with its cautionary, editorial and parentheses attributes.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: a model of which accidentals are displayed was wrong on 8,543 of 76,813 file-accidental notes (11.1%) against OpenSheetMusicDisplay's render, so the display layer is out of this batch. music21 raised 'incorrect accidental' on one old file (Mozart K. 545 alt). music21 Pitch.accidental.displayStatus exists but reading it as 'printed' is unverified.
pitfalls: Exporters that omit <accidental> for printed accidentals or add redundant ones; the count is the file's claim, not the page.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: bar with F-sharp then F-natural, both with <accidental> -> 1 sharp, 1 natural. Fail: a C major scale -> 0. Fool: an F-sharp tied over the barline with no <accidental> on the second note -> counted once (as encoded).
in_our_files: all files (element counts not yet taken)
used_for: A.5 (sharps and flats), 1.1 (occasional accidentals), reading difficulty (accidental rate, one of Sébastien et al.'s seven criteria), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read once the display question is left out.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT AS NARROW FACT — Count explicit `<accidental>` tokens by printed type and position; distinguish this carefully from the effective altered sounding pitch and from the renderer’s displayed accidentals. MusicXML allows cautionary/editorial/parentheses markers, and accidentals may also be attached to grace/cue notes; record these flags. Deliberately returning zero for an implied but unencoded natural is right for this *encoded* fact, not evidence the reader sees none.
implementation_observed: music21 Pitch.accidental.displayStatus for encoded sign tokens; targeted raw XML for cautionary/editorial flags; per staff/grace counts and top bars.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Good hybrid if raw flags genuinely lost by music21; no need to recreate full accidental renderer.
correctness_and_musical_risks: displayStatus is an importer-derived display intention, not literal proof every <accidental> token survived import; raw flag totals do not apply _notes filter to cue/slash heads or chord-member-level print control and can diverge from kinds totals. Grouped bar labels may collide at repeats; per-bar_index mitigates.
test_quality_and_unverified: Header spot probes only; check editorial-only, cautionary, duplicated chord sign, hidden/slash note, grace and nonstandard accidentals. No validation against raw token count across corpus here.
recommended_correction: Reconcile music21 sign count against raw <accidental> tokens on corpus; mark non-round-tripped varieties, and scope raw flags with same print policy.
code_evidence: accidentals(); a.displayStatus; part.iter('note') flags; _notes.printed
claude_ruling: PARTLY. The raw cautionary/editorial counts already skip hidden notes; slash heads carry no accidentals in our files (239, one file). Reconcile music21 against raw <accidental> totals on the corpus: LATER (one script).

fact: Notes the key signature actually alters
reports: For each key-signature span: which of the signature's altered letters occur with the signature's alteration, and how often.
definition: A note counts when its step is one the signature alters and its alter equals the signature's alter for that step (e.g. F-sharp under one sharp). Notes carrying a different alter (an F-natural) do not count.
implementation: music21 KeySignature.accidentalByStep(step) compared with each note's pitch.accidental alter, per key span from E06; or the same from raw <step>/<alter>.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: implemented in the app detector (keySignature, detect.ts line 532) but measured only through its failing display model. music21 alteredPitches ran on Maple Leaf Rag (B-flat, E-flat, A-flat, D-flat); the per-note comparison was not run.
pitfalls: Non-traditional keys; a signature with no affected notes (e.g. a G major piece with no F at all) is a real result, not an error.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: G major melody with F-sharps -> F-sharp counted. Fail: G major piece without any F -> 0 (signature not exercised). Fool: an F-natural with an explicit natural in G major -> not counted.
used_for: B.4 and 1.12 (key signatures met in pieces), step 4 generator check (an exercise in G that uses F-sharp)
why_easy: One comparison per note from library values.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The signature-altered pitch count is useful, but written `<alter>` can be omitted on notes that sound under a current key (depending on export). Resolve effective pitch from key signature and explicit accidental context rather than assuming every F-sharp has `<alter>1</alter>`; verify the input convention empirically first. A single chromatic natural on an F must not count. Compare signature state over mid-piece changes and separate changed-note counts from simply having the signature.
implementation_observed: Counts struck notes whose pitch step/alter matches currently encoded key-signature alteration; groups under signature string.
implementation_and_library_reuse: music21 KeySignature.accidentalByStep and pitches are appropriate; no custom accidental-state emulator.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Critical definition mismatch: docstring promises 'per written signature (span)' but dict keyed only by signature (e.g., '2') merges every separate appearance of that signature in the piece and across staves. No bar locations or span boundaries; cannot locate teaching examples or distinguish signature change/reintroduction. If alteredPitches exists but an alteration is absent on some affected notes, the 189 unexplained cases are silently missed. Minor-signature mode ignored intentionally but needs labeling.
test_quality_and_unverified: Reported 842-file raw comparison only in comment, not replicated; test K=C->G->C->G and staff-specific key signatures, natural cancellations.
recommended_correction: Emit a list of identified signature spans per staff with bar indices, letter use and unresolved encoding cases; keep aggregate if useful but not mislabeled 'per span'.
code_evidence: name=str(ks.sharps) ...; used[name][...]; letters.setdefault(name,..)
claude_ruling: AGREE that 'per span' was mislabelled. FIXED: docstring and comment now say per signature with all its spans merged. Per-span locations: LATER, only if a consumer needs them.

fact: Time signatures, changes and metre class
reports: Each signature with its bar; number of changes; class of each: simple (2, 3, 4 beats), compound (numerator 6, 9 or 12 over 4, 8 or 16), irregular (5, 7, 11 and others, and composite numerators like 3+2); 'no time signature' when absent.
definition: A change is a signature different from the one in force. Class from the numerator and denominator only, by the rule above (6/4 is compound duple; 3/8 is simple triple). Grouping of irregular metres (2+3 or 3+2) is not decided unless the numerator is written as a sum.
implementation: Raw <time><beats>/<beat-type> (with <senza-misura> and symbol attributes); music21 meter.TimeSignature.classification as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: music21 and partitura plain reads equal the raw reader on all 187 changes in 49 items. Gnossienne No. 1 has no <time>; partitura returns an empty list. Old detector problems were in classing a change as a device or pickup, not in reading it.
pitfalls: Restatements; a pickup written as its own short signature at the start (reported as 'possible pickup signature'); cadenza bars; cut and common time symbols (read the numbers, keep the symbol).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 6/8 -> compound; 3/4 then 2/4 at bar 9 -> 1 change. Fail: 4/4 throughout -> 0 changes, simple. Fool: 4/4 restated at bar 17 -> 0 changes; 3/8 -> simple, not compound.
used_for: A.3 (2/4), B.2 (a change of time signature), 1.4 (6/8), 3.3 (12/8 and changing metres), 6.7 (9/8, 5/8, 5/4), 7.8 (7/8, 7/4), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; two libraries matched the raw reader on every change tested.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Record actual `<beats>` (including additive strings) and `<beat-type>` first. The division into simple/compound is a conventional interpretation, not always determined by integer numerator/denominator alone; 6/4 can be subdivided in multiple ways. Preserve ambiguous/alternating/senza-misura cases and beaming/grouping evidence rather than asserting an unequivocal beat unit. 3/8 not compound by itself is a useful fix. Tests need a 6/4 with 3+3 vs 2+2+2 grouping and an additive meter.
implementation_observed: music21 TimeSignature per staff; custom conservative simple/compound/UNKNOWN; raw first-part senza-misura.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Appropriate music21 for explicit markings; caution with own metrical grouping inferred from numerator.
correctness_and_musical_risks: DEDUP BUG: seen key (bar_index, sig) excludes offset and staff; two changes to the same signature at different positions in one bar collapse. `change` field derived from staff-specific prev but stored globally on first encounter; can classify actual change as initial. Senza-misura is only first part. Meter classification 9/4 or 12/4 compound is an interpretation, not certain from notation.
test_quality_and_unverified: Need in-bar multiple signatures, staff-only changes, senza-misura in later part, irregular additive meters; claimed probes not rerun.
recommended_correction: Merge by bar index+offset+written signature, preserve each staff's timeline, expose ambiguous grouping and number of changes per staff.
code_evidence: times(): key=(index.get(id(meas)),sig); `seen`; _class()
claude_ruling: AGREE: real bug. FIXED: the merge key is now bar + offset + signature, each entry has its offset, and a test with 3/4 changing to 2/4 inside one bar passes.

reports: Whether the first bar is shorter than the signature, its length, the implicit flag, and the last bar's length (a classical pickup is often balanced by a short last bar).
definition: First measure's notated length (E02) less than the time signature's length, or measure@implicit='yes'. Both lengths are reported; nothing else is decided.
implementation: From E02. music21 Measure.paddingLeft as the second reader (corpus Maple Leaf Rag bar 0: paddingLeft 1.5, duration 0.5 of 2.0).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated on 5 named items (Away in a Manger one quarter of 3/4; Alexander's Ragtime Band 2 of 4; Für Elise one eighth of 3/8; two full-bar starts).
pitfalls: A first bar that is short only because a rest was omitted looks like a pickup; the implicit flag is reported so the two cases can be told apart where the file sets it.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: Away in a Manger (shortlist file 002) -> 1 quarter of 3. Fail: a piece starting on a full bar -> no pickup. Fool: first bar with one voice full and the other missing its rest -> full (largest voice).
used_for: A.3 (the upbeat), reading rungs, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Comes free from E02.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — A short first bar is a *pickup candidate*, not always a real anacrusis; corrupt/incomplete transcription and cadenza can mimic it. Conversely `<measure implicit="yes">` may be exporter metadata, not a trustworthy pickup by itself. Report both independent observations; establish actual pickup when they agree or score context supports it. Include displaced pickup time for offset-based detectors and a last-bar complement check when present, without inventing one as a hard rule.
implementation_observed: Combines E02 first/last durations and raw implicit flag with music21 paddingLeft; candidate and confirmed flags.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Reasonable reuse; little custom logic.
correctness_and_musical_risks: 'confirmed' is not justified solely by two exporter/structural cues: first-short+implicit may be a fragment or implicit-layout choice, first-short+complement may arise by coincidence. Could misleadingly certify a true pickup. Uses first score part padding rather than first active pitched staff. 8va etc irrelevant.
test_quality_and_unverified: Check true pickup with full ending, first clipped/cadenza, short last unrelated, and absent time. No printed-score check.
recommended_correction: Rename 'confirmed' to 'supported_pickup'/'strong_candidate'; preserve raw observations and uncertainty, leaving printed-score certification to review.
code_evidence: pickup(): confirmed = short_first and (first['implicit'] or complements)
claude_ruling: PARTLY. Agree 'confirmed' means two file observations agree, not a printed check; FIXED in the comment. Kept the key name because E32 reads it.

fact: Note and rest values, dots and ties, per staff
reports: Per staff: counts of notes and of rests by written type (whole to 32nd and shorter), dotted and double-dotted counts, tie chains (count, how many cross a barline), the shortest written value, and bars where the written type disagrees with the duration.
definition: Written <type> and <dot> of each non-grace, non-cue note and rest; a tie chain is a run of notes linked by <tie type='start'/'stop'> (two tied notes are one chain, two written notes).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 duration.type and dots as the second reader; ties from <tie> (sound) with <tied> (notation) as a check.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: values validated over 2,020 files; every value shorter than a 128th sat in a bar that also carries a quantisation ratio (a PDMX re-export artefact); cue-size notes kept in 26 files. music21 and partitura agreed on tie starts in a corpus file (4 and 4).
pitfalls: Notes without <type> (derive from duration and report); cue notes; re-export artefacts with odd values (reported, not used for difficulty); grace notes are counted in E14, not here.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: bar of four eighths -> 4 eighths. Fail: bar of half notes -> no eighths. Fool: a quarter tied to an eighth -> one quarter, one eighth, one tie chain; not a dotted quarter.
used_for: A.3 (rests, eighths), B.2 (eighth patterns), 2.4 (sixteenths), level fit (no sixteenths at B), difficulty (shortest value, share of short values), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; replaces the duration counting in rung_pieces.py with a tested one.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Printed duration `<type>/<dot>` and performed/encoded `<duration>` are different facts; keep both. MusicXML uses both `<tie>` playback and `<notations><tied>` engraving, which can disagree; do not rely on only `<tie>`. Tuplets, chords, rests, cross-bar chains and rearticulated same-pitch notes need separate treatment. The basic parsing is easy, but tie-chain reconstruction requires note identity by staff/voice/pitch and appropriate ambiguity handling.
implementation_observed: music21 duration.type,dots,linked, ties and measure rests; raw cue mark count; distinct shortest struck type and barline tie crossings.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Good reuse; narrow raw cue extraction plausibly justified.
correctness_and_musical_risks: `notes_by_type` increments once per chord EVENT while raw 'small_notes' counts individual note heads; denominator semantics inconsistent across rows. It does not filter slash noteheads although _notes says all pitch counting follows that rule. Counts tie chains from every member; tie stop/continue for `<tied>`-only ignored (documented 10). A barline crossing counted only when continuation at onset zero; ties crossing after pickup/grouping may not be represented at offset 0. `Duration.linked == False` is not a universal proof of encoded/type mismatch.
test_quality_and_unverified: Run mix of chord members, slash/hidden, note duration altered by tuplet, tied crossbar, typed/untagged full rests; measured corpus note counts not independently rerun.
recommended_correction: Make note events vs noteheads explicit, reuse _notes.printed for pitch-bearing counts, separate notated ties from playback ties where they disagree; compare genuine raw written duration when needed.
code_evidence: values(): notes[d.type]+=1; members excludes only hideObject; cross += at0; mismatch += not d.linked
claude_ruling: PARTLY. notes_by_type counts note EVENTS (a chord once) while small_notes counts heads: FIXED in the docstring. Slash heads stay in this RHYTHM row on purpose (a slash shows a rhythm). Duration.linked False is music21's own type/duration-mismatch flag (probed). NO OTHER CHANGE.

reports: Per staff: count and bars of dotted quarter followed by an eighth, and of dotted eighth followed by a sixteenth, in simple metres.
definition: Two consecutive notes or rests in the same voice and staff: (dotted quarter, eighth) or (dotted eighth, sixteenth), in a bar whose metre class (E09) is simple. In compound time a dotted quarter is the beat, not the figure, so compound bars are excluded.
implementation: Per-voice sequence from the raw walk or music21; pairs read from E11 values.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old app detector (dottedQuarters, detect.ts line 416) counted simple time only; validated on 4 items (Für Elise 12 dotted-eighth pairs). rung_pieces.py already counts both figures without the simple-time rule.
pitfalls: The eighth before the dotted quarter (reverse figure) is a different figure and not counted; a dotted quarter tied into an eighth.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 4/4 bar 'dotted quarter, eighth, half' -> 1. Fail: even quarters -> 0. Fool: 6/8 bar of two dotted quarters -> 0.
used_for: B.2 (dotted quarter-eighth), 2.4 (dotted eighth-sixteenth), step 4 generator check
why_easy: A pair lookup over E11 with one metre condition.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Report dotted pairs only for adjacent actual *note onsets* in one voice, and optionally corresponding rest+note rhythmic cells as a separate kind. The current definition includes rests as interchangeable with notes, which can invent the wrong pedagogical pattern. A dotted-quarter/eighth may occur in various meters, so exclude compound only if this row specifically means a simple-time teaching figure; do not suppress the underlying dotted value (E11). Test ties, dotted-quarter plus rest, and voice interleaving.
implementation_observed: music21 voice sequence checks adjacent dotted/short notes in simple time, with then-rest separate.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Good reuse of parsed voices and durations; custom relation is small and defined.
correctness_and_musical_risks: A.isRest is explicitly excluded (good). Gap relation and no-tie continuation handle ordinary figures, but a dotted first note tied forward is still counted even if next is a new attack not continuation? Usually fine. Excludes all a.duration.tuplets, consistent with narrow row. `where` ignores rest variants and has no offsets; can conceal location. Hidden notes filtered via object style, not member-level slash policy. Intra-voice event order in complex cross-staff notation should be verified.
test_quality_and_unverified: Edge tests require chord+rest, tie, tuplet, 6/8, empty voice, and cross-bar false; no score-level tests verified.
recommended_correction: Keep; label counts as same-voice written rhythmic figures, store bar indices/offsets and optionally rest variant locations.
code_evidence: dotted(): for a,b in zip(seq,seq[1:]); FIG; a.offset+a.quarterLength==b.offset
claude_ruling: AGREE minor points; NO CHANGE (bar labels are enough to find the figure).

reports: Per staff: groups by ratio (3:2, 6:4, 5:4, 2:3 duplets and others), notes per group, bars.
definition: A group is a printed bracket: <tuplet type='start'> ... <tuplet type='stop'> enclosing 2 or more notes whose <time-modification> ratio is not 1. Ratios on notes with no bracket element are not counted (see evidence).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 duration.tuplets as the second reader (corpus Clara Schumann Op. 1 No. 1: music21 66 notes at 3:2; partitura 22 groups; they agree).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: raw <time-modification> alone included re-export artefacts (77 distinct ratios, e.g. 160:107); reading only closed brackets of 2 or more notes kept 14 of 14 real figures and dropped 21 of 21 artefacts, and lost 1 of 231 3:2 groups.
pitfalls: Unclosed brackets (10 in the old catalogue); nested tuplets; files that encode triplets with ratios but no <tuplet> element (missed by this definition; reported as 'unbracketed ratios' for review).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: three eighths under a 3:2 bracket -> one triplet group. Fail: plain eighths -> 0. Fool: a 160:107 ratio with no bracket -> 0 groups, listed under unbracketed ratios.
used_for: 1.4 (triplets), 2.4 (triplets), BL.4 (triplet licks), 6.7 (triplets in reading), difficulty (tuplet share; one of Sébastien et al.'s criteria), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read with the artefact rule the old project already measured.
chatgpt_independent_review: REQUIRED CHANGE — A tuplet is not synonymous with a printed bracket. MusicXML `<time-modification>` can specify triplets with no `<notations><tuplet>` bracket, including common unbracketed triplets; the present definition would miss those. Detect tuplets from effective time modification, report ratio, count and onset coverage, and separately report bracket signs if printed. Add adversarial unbracketed, nested, incomplete and two-voice tuplets. This is a material false-negative risk for rhythm lessons.
implementation_observed: Hybrid music21 Duration.tuplets for spans/runs, raw time-modification ratio for written 6:4 etc; suspect filters ratios.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Strong reason for raw written ratio when music21 reduces equivalent ratios; music21 still handles grouping/voice.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Arbitrary plausible() limits 2..12 and 0.5 < ratio <2 reject legitimate unusual tuplet ratios (e.g. 3:2 okay, 2:1 excluded; 13:8 excluded); correctly marked suspect as long as not treated as proof not a tuplet. Raw per-staff ratio omits chord notehead print condition and may overcount chord continuation. `runs` resets at each bar even if tuplet spans bars; adjacent tuplet same ratio may merge when no printed type=start, while bracket groups can be nested. Printed bracket count uses music21 `.bracket` metadata, which can be None for unspecified visual default.
test_quality_and_unverified: Header has concrete corpus gap evidence; need unbracketed 3:2, 6:4, multi-bar, nested, 2:1, >12, and string of adjoining identical tuplets.
recommended_correction: Do not make plausible() a truth criterion for whether written tuplets exist; report all written nontrivial ratios, separately flag probable re-export artefacts with explicitly heuristic label; distinguish group/bracket and bar-local run counts.
code_evidence: plausible(a,n); tuplets(); r=(t[0].numberNotesActual,..); `prev` reset each measure
claude_ruling: PARTLY. The plausibility rule never says 'not a tuplet': other ratios are reported under suspect, as ChatGPT asks. Runs reset at the barline (a tuplet across a bar counts twice): LATER, rare.

chatgpt_ids: mark.ornament (grace part); texture.crushed-note (the grace note only)
reports: Per staff: count, slashed (acciaccatura) versus unslashed (appoggiatura), runs of consecutive grace notes and their longest length, bars.
definition: Notes with a <grace> element; slash='yes' marks the slashed kind. A run is consecutive grace notes before one main note.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 duration.isGrace as the second reader (corpus Clara Schumann Op. 1 No. 3: 39 in both music21 and partitura). Do not use partitura's note_array with grace notes included (it crashed in 1.9.0).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: 247 real items carry <grace>; runs of 6 or more occur in Chopin files (written-out flourishes).
pitfalls: Cue-size notes that are not <grace>; long grace runs are a different thing from an ornamental grace note and are reported as runs.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: one slashed grace before a quarter -> 1 slashed. Fail: no <grace> -> 0. Fool: small cue-size notes without <grace> -> 0.
used_for: 2.6 (grace notes), 3.4 (appoggiatura), BL.6 (crushed notes), difficulty, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; two libraries agreed on the corpus test.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — `<grace>` is direct; report slash attribute, run length and which main note follows. A grace cluster can span an onset/voice boundary, so pair by part/staff/voice in score order instead of treating mere XML adjacency as musical attachment. Do not infer acciaccatura/appoggiatura stylistic execution from the slash alone. Good easy score fact.
implementation_observed: music21 GraceDuration per voice, raw grace slash attribute per staff due documented import mismatch.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Reasonable music21-first + small measured gap fix.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Critical semantic bug: a run of grace notes at the END of a bar is classified as 'after_run' when it can lead INTO the first main note of the next bar; grouping resets per bar. A grace run preceding another voice's anchor might also be misattributed. Per-grace head count and raw slash token count differ intentionally but names do not clarify head vs event. Bars list omits trailing grace runs, except count.
test_quality_and_unverified: Test grace cluster crossing measure boundary and voice change, chord with mixed size, repeated slash defaults; compare score playback only if relevant.
recommended_correction: Build voice sequence across measures to attach grace run to next main event, classify true after-note vs pending/cross-bar as UNKNOWN; keep marks as printed facts.
code_evidence: grace(): for meas ... for v ... run=0; `if run` at end increments `after`
claude_ruling: AGREE: real bug. FIXED: a grace run at the end of a bar is carried to the next bar's first main note in the same voice (runs_across_barline counts them); after_runs now means no later main note at all. Two tests added.

reports: Per staff: counts by kind (trill-mark, wavy-line without a trill mark, mordent, inverted mordent, turn, inverted or delayed turn, schleifer, shake, other), bars.
definition: Children of <notations><ornaments>; <tremolo> inside ornaments is E17, not here.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 note.expressions (Trill, Mordent, InvertedMordent, Turn, ...) as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 3: Turn 5, Trill 2).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no measured finding for ornament signs; a SMuFL glyph was once misread as a fingering. rung_pieces.py counts ornaments without kinds.
pitfalls: 'tr' typed as <words>; <other-ornament> with a SMuFL glyph (reported as other).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a trill mark on a half note -> 1 trill. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'tr' as <words> -> 0 trills, listed under text.
in_our_files: trill-mark 129 (15.3%), mordent 42 (5.0%), inverted mordent 89 (10.6%), turn 17 (2.0%) of 842
used_for: 3.4 (trill, mordent), difficulty, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH SCOPE — Detect exact ornament element tags, position and line/spanner extent, with one count for signs and another for written-out ornament realizations (not covered here). Mark custom/unknown ornament names unknown, and do not treat the sign as proof of correct ornament execution. Test trills with wavy lines and variants of mordent/turn signs.
implementation_observed: Typed music21 Ornament subclasses on printed notes; music21 TrillExtension for wavy-line-only, separate tr text token.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Strong library reuse; no reinvented ornament classifier.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Known ignored vertical-turn/haydn and rest-anchored trills mean counts aren't exhaustive as notated signs, contrary to broad name. TrillExtension counted without location or hidden-state check for full span; score-level spanner storage may escape staff-local traversal. `printed` excludes slash and hidden by design. Text 'tr' can have more than one spelling.
test_quality_and_unverified: 4 corpus discrepancy examples and importer losses asserted. Need cross-check rare symbol tag handling and rest-attached ornament; decide whether those ever matter for rungs.
recommended_correction: Document supported ornament vocabulary and known misses, mark uncertain rather than manufacturing counts; no broad custom fallback unless real rung material requires it.
code_evidence: ornaments(): m.expressions subclass tuple; TrillExtension; TR_WORD.fullmatch
claude_ruling: AGREE. Known misses (vertical-turn, haydn, trills on rests) are listed in the comment. NO CHANGE.

reports: Per staff: chords with <arpeggiate> (direction when given) and with <non-arpeggiate>, bars.
definition: <notations><arpeggiate> on any note of a chord marks that chord.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.ArpeggioMark as the second reader (ran on corpus Op. 1 No. 1: 6).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding (its 'arpeggio' rule was a broken-chord pattern, a different thing).
pitfalls: Arpeggio spanning both staves (one sign per staff in the file).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: wavy line on a 4-note chord -> 1. Fail: plain chord -> 0. Fool: a broken chord written out in eighths -> 0 (that is a pattern, not the sign).
used_for: E37 (a wide chord marked to be rolled is not a stretch), difficulty, 8.4 performance marks
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH GROUPING FIX — An `<arpeggiate>` sign often appears on multiple chord notes; deduplicate by event/group number, staff and onset to avoid counting one rolled chord three times. Preserve direction and `<non-arpeggiate>` indications as distinct facts, with cross-staff grouping possible. The sign requests a spread, but E36 same-onset notes do not cease being a notated chord.
implementation_observed: music21 ArpeggioMark and ArpeggioMarkSpanner, grouped by same staff/time into one rolled chord.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Appropriate library-first with well-argued group-by-onset correction for parallel voices.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Coalesces DISTINCT arpeggiation groups at same onset/staff, including different numbered group signs and opposite directions; counts as one. A cross-staff roll appears in per-staff results and may be double-counted at aggregate. ArpeggioMarkSpanner stored at score level may be outside staff recursion; spanned mapping is score-level so good. Grouping lacks number identity due importer.
test_quality_and_unverified: Check two simultaneous arpeggio groups on same staff, cross-staff one sign vs two, nonarpeggiate mixed group; corpus Schumann example asserted only.
recommended_correction: Preserve (if available) notation group number / span identity; if impossible, label merged onset groups as approximate rather than exact roll count; avoid double counting cross-staff roll.
code_evidence: arpeggiate(): `rolls[(mi,Fraction(offset))]`, any kinds -> 1 c['arpeggiated_chords']
claude_ruling: PARTLY. Grouping by staff+onset is deliberate (fixes 30 marks -> 15 printed rolls in Schumann Op. 68/30); two different rolls at one onset on one staff is the price, rare. No aggregate across staves exists, so no double count. LATER: label as onset-grouped.

reports: Per staff: single-note and two-note tremolos with number of strokes, bars.
definition: <ornaments><tremolo type='single|start|stop|unmeasured'>; the text value is the number of strokes.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.Tremolo as the second reader (ran on corpus Op. 1 No. 4: 24).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: read through partitura ornaments; no measured count.
pitfalls: Measured repeated notes written out (that is E40's repeated notes, not a tremolo sign).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: three-stroke tremolo on a half note -> 1 single, 3 strokes. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: written-out 32nd repetitions -> 0.
used_for: BL.6 (tremolo), difficulty
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Report `<tremolo>` strokes and type; pair two-note start/stop across notes and distinguish single-note measured repetitions from two-note alternations. Not all strokes imply an unmeasured trill-like performance; keep printed value and style separate. Include unpaired start, one-note tremolo, two-note tremolo and tremolo versus beams.
implementation_observed: music21 single-note Tremolo expressions and TremoloSpanner for two-note alternations.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Direct library application; no need custom parser unless missing cases matter.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Unmatched start/stop silently excluded and zero strokes accepted, acknowledged in header; two-note spanners searched per staff and may miss score-level/cross-staff spans. One hidden endpoint can still count two-note spanner because only first checked. Bars carry only label, not precise start/end.
test_quality_and_unverified: Check spanner storage and cross-staff, hidden second endpoint, unpaired mark; standard music21 object behavior not independently run.
recommended_correction: Preserve import limitations and report UNKNOWN/orphans if actual repertoire uses malformed tremolos; test score-level spanner capture.
code_evidence: tremolo(): for sp in staff.recurse().getElementsByClass(TremoloSpanner); first.style.hideObjectOnPrint
claude_ruling: AGREE minor. NO CHANGE (19 files have tremolos).

reports: Per staff: glissando and slide spans with start and end notes, bars; 'gliss.' words listed separately.
definition: <notations><glissando> and <slide> start/stop pairs.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 spanner.Glissando as the second reader (only tested on a constructed object; no corpus piano file has one).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding.
pitfalls: 'gliss.' typed as words with no span; a span with no stop.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a glissando from C4 to C6 -> 1 span. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'gliss.' as words only -> 0 spans, listed as text.
used_for: 3.4 (glissando)
why_easy: Direct read; rare, so low value.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Match glissando and slide start/stop by number and kind, with staff and in-measure time. Prefer a source-location + intended target rather than assuming paired notes are always in one staff. A written text "gliss." with no MusicXML spanner stays text/unclassified; distinguish encoded black-key/white-key instruction if available.
implementation_observed: music21 Glissando spanners; preserves two endpoints and distinguishes slides, plus unstructured words.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Strong direct library reuse.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Labels `glissando` for any slideType other than 'continuous', including unknown; classifies 'continuous' as slide by assumption importer mapping. Does not check ending note print-hidden. Scope to two note endpoints, not technique. Small number of actual candidates means edge cases not broad.
test_quality_and_unverified: Constructed objects and four actual slide case claim; test literal MusicXML slide versus glissando, cross-staff, unmatched endpoints, hidden end.
recommended_correction: Keep library route; unknown slideType should be UNKNOWN and support `end` not printed flag; no further feature build without use case.
code_evidence: glissando(): g.slideType == 'continuous' else glissando; start/end from getSpannedElements
claude_ruling: AGREE. FIXED: only 'chromatic' -> glissando and 'continuous' -> slide; anything else is UNKNOWN.

reports: Fermatas on notes, rests and barlines, with bar and staff.
definition: <notations><fermata> on a note or rest, and <barline><fermata>.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.Fermata as the second reader (ran on corpus Schoenberg Op. 19/2: 2).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: read through partitura; no measured count.
pitfalls: The same fermata written on both staves (count per staff and per time position).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: fermata on the final chord -> 1. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: fermata on both staves at the same beat -> 1 time position, 2 marks.
used_for: A.6 (fermata), tempo-change list (E26)
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT — Direct token extraction from notes, rests and barlines is straightforward. Report shape (`upright`/`inverted` where encoded) and position; not duration in seconds. The same sign may attach to several notes in a chord, so distinguish mark-token count and musical-pause location. Include repeat/end-barline fermata and chords.
implementation_observed: music21 Fermata expressions on notes/rests; targeted raw read for barline fermata.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Justified narrow hybrid; nice distinction mark-count vs shared pause location.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Barline raw read only first part, may omit independent staff/part fermatas. No shape by design; acknowledged importer inconsistency, but a minimal raw flag would preserve encoded shape if needed. Distinct 'time_positions' excludes barline signs, even though both may represent pauses. Assumption two staff at same bar/offset is one pause is plausible but not always.

reports: Each mark (pppp to ffff, mp, mf, sf, sfz, sffz, fz, fp, rf, rfz, other) with bar and staff; the set of levels used; softest and loudest; time positions where the two staves have different dynamics.
definition: Children of <direction><direction-type><dynamics> (staff from the direction's <staff>) and of <notations><dynamics>. Words such as 'dolce' or 'cresc.' are not dynamics.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 dynamics.Dynamic as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 1: mf 3, f 3, p 1). Do not use partitura for this: it classed the word 'calando' as a dynamic.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: sf, sfz and fz counts read through partitura equalled the raw counts (Moonlight III 49, Hall of the Mountain King 39).
pitfalls: Dynamics typed as words ('p dolce'); <other-dynamics>; a direction without a staff number (applies to staff 1).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: p at bar 1 and f at bar 9 -> 2 marks, range p to f. Fail: none -> empty. Fool: 'dolce' words -> not a dynamic.
used_for: A.6 (loud and soft), B.8 (pp), 1.6 (mp, mf), 3.4 (sforzando), 7.4 (different dynamics in each hand), difficulty, step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Parse structured `<dynamics>` both in directions and notations, but do not assume each is on a determinable staff: staff may be omitted, placed between staves, or spread over a group. Preserve `staff_unspecified` rather than defaulting to staff 1. Written `sfz`, `fp`, `rfz` are not directly comparable on one ppp–fff numerical scale. Separate written symbol from measured performance dynamic and from generic expressive words.
implementation_observed: music21 Dynamic by staff, levels/accent categories and simultaneous mismatched levels across two staves.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Appropriate library-first; documented corpus explanation for not parsing raw staff omission.
correctness_and_musical_risks: 'staves differ at' only tests simultaneous dynamic *markings*, not differing active written dynamic levels over a passage; may miss different markings given at different times. No initial unspecific staff parsing; falls apart on out-of-corpus input where music21 duplicates unspecified directions. Values named 'other' lose actual other-dynamics text; sign could be parsed raw if teaching specifically needs it. Level classification excludes sf etc intentionally.
test_quality_and_unverified: Test staggered piano/forte marking, no-staff directions, dynamic in notations, 'other-dynamics'; limited corpus does not prove general behavior.
recommended_correction: Rename count as 'simultaneous conflicting dynamic marks', not broader staff dynamics independence; flag ambiguous staff and support nonstandard marks only when needed.
code_evidence: dynamics(): differ counts equal (bar_index,offset) pairs, not persistent dynamic state
claude_ruling: AGREE. FIXED: the key is now conflicting_marks_same_moment (marks at one moment, not levels in force over a passage).

reports: Wedges (crescendo, diminuendo) with staff and bars; 'cresc.', 'dim.', 'decresc.' words listed separately with bars.

implementation: Raw walk; music21 dynamics.Crescendo and Diminuendo as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 1: 2 crescendos). partitura found none on the same file, so it is not used.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: crescendo read through partitura; diminuendo apparently missing there.
pitfalls: Unclosed wedges; a wedge on one staff meant for both.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a crescendo wedge over bars 3-4 -> 1. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'cresc.' words -> 0 wedges, 1 word.
used_for: A.6, B.8 and 1.6 (crescendo, diminuendo, hairpins), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; music21 matched on the corpus test.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Distinguish wedge spanners (numbered start/stop, `continue` where present) from crescendo/diminuendo words and retain ambiguous/unmatched text. A word is a label, not an inferred duration span unless anchored by explicit markup; do not fabricate a fade interval after "cresc.". Keep numbered overlapping hairpins, directions without staff and words like `cresc. poco a poco` as test cases.
implementation_observed: Raw wedge event extraction/time pairing, music21 TextExpressions for cresc./dim words.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Custom pairing has documented cases where music21 10.5 pairs wrong, so justified if raw pairing is actually more accurate; uses shared generic XML helper rather than unrelated parser.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Ignores MusicXML `wedge type=continue`, while claims reporting spans; cannot represent continuation segments; FIFO pairing of overlapping same-number marks remains uncertain. Labels from first staff for all parts. Raw timing inherits int(float) offset truncation. Words are not assigned time/staff, limiting teaching locations.
test_quality_and_unverified: Header cites concrete QmUaMY/Qmbm31 examples, but no independently verified engraved result. Test same-bar stop/start, overlaps, continue, and time subdivisions.
recommended_correction: Handle `continue` explicitly, retain words with bar location, mark overlapping ambiguous pairs, fix `_raw.directions` exact offsets before trusting boundaries.
code_evidence: hairpins(): typ in ('crescendo','diminuendo','stop'); pair_spans(events); words list only content
claude_ruling: PARTLY. continue: same as ottava, intermediate, fine for complete spans. Offsets: FIXED via _raw.directions. Pairing improved (FIFO, measured). Words without location: LATER.

reports: Per staff: counts by kind (staccato, staccatissimo, tenuto, detached-legato, accent, strong accent, spiccato, breath mark, other), bars.
