implementation: Raw walk; music21 note.articulations as the second reader (corpus Op. 1 No. 1: staccato 12, accent 8 in music21 and partitura alike).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: accents read through partitura (accent items 101 PDMX).
pitfalls: Articulations typed as words; a staccato on every note of a chord counted once per chord (report both).
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: four staccato quarters -> 4 staccatos. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: a 3-note chord with one staccato -> 1 chord.
used_for: A.2 (staccato), A.6 and 1.6 (accents), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; two libraries agreed.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT — Report exact articulation tags and note/staff position, with compound/articulation glyph variants retained. A `staccato` mark is a requested touch, not a proven staccato note duration in performance. Keep notations attached to multiple chord notes from being mistaken for multiple independent attacks. Add adversarial tenuto+staccato and jazz-specific tags.
implementation_observed: music21 exact-class articulation map (`ARTICULATION_MARKS`), counts printed notated attacks, combinations, duplicates, grace and tie-continuation signs.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Excellent reuse and unusually strong importer-vs-raw corpus comparison in header; no raw reader is duplicated for the ~6 documented lost marks.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Music21 collapses chord-member attachments, but corpus evidence says no significant loss. Includes tie continuations in metric named attacks, explicitly disclosed, whereas E36 attack counters exclude them: cross-row percentages are not directly comparable. `ARTICULATION_MARKS` internal library mapping is version-sensitive; soft-accent and rare signs lost.
test_quality_and_unverified: Dedicated test_e22 covers subclass confusions, duplicates, hidden, grace, chord and import limitations; raw 842-file comparison is claimed in comments, not independently rerun.
recommended_correction: Keep library implementation; label denominator 'printed note/chord events (including tie continuations)' rather than sounding attacks, and version-pin music21 mapping. Do not add new parser for rare six marks without need.
code_evidence: type(a) in kind_of derived from music21.musicxml.xmlObjects.ARTICULATION_MARKS; `attacks += 1`; comment ~747,754 corpus notes
claude_ruling: AGREE. The denominator is already labelled (attacks include tie continuations, as E23/E27). Pin music21 10.5: LATER (README note). NO CODE CHANGE.

reports: Per staff: number of slurs, notes under slurs (share of all notes), average notes per slur, bars; slurs that join two notes of the same pitch listed separately (likely a mis-encoded tie).
definition: <slur type='start|stop' number> paired by number within a staff and voice.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 spanner.Slur as the second reader.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding. rung_pieces.py counts music21 Slur objects in the bars used.
pitfalls: Dangling starts or stops; slurs crossing staves; same-pitch slurs.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: a slur over four notes -> 1 slur, 4 notes. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: a 'slur' between two Cs of the same pitch -> listed as possible tie.
used_for: A.2 (legato), B.8 (phrase marks), 1.6 (slurs), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Slur identity is scoped by MusicXML number within the relevant part and staff context, but spanning notes may change voice; hard-keying both staff and voice can strand legitimate slurs. Capture source/target notes, number, position and ambiguity with tests for overlapping slurs and cross-voice starts/stops. Do not equate slur to successful legato, phrasing or a note-by-note fingering recommendation.
implementation_observed: Own 320-line raw slur-mark cursor/pairer with music21 for printed attacked notes. Matches by part/number and ranks starts by voice/staff; nearest-attack snapping with 1/16 quarter tolerance; computes share of notes under slurs.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Real evidence presented that music21 mishandles cross-staff, in-bar out-of-document-order, incomplete and overlapping slurs; custom fallback is defensible, but this is a substantial replacement of musical-structure pairing, not a trivial XML patch. Complexity needs proportionality to lesson use.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Undocumented truth is still ambiguous: matching 'latest' among equal-ranked starts can silently choose incorrect one; ambiguous flags don't identify individual corrected spans. Hard-coded EPS=1/100 and SNAP=1/16 quarter may snap a mark to wrong nearby attack. Voice-matching by imported ID can splice parts; no per-slur endpoints supplied despite claiming comprehensive musical details. `_slur_marks` uses int(float(xml duration)) cursor. Slurs do not automatically mean legato or phrases.
test_quality_and_unverified: test_e23 has extensive hand cases, including music21 failures, overlapping numbers, cross staff/voice, snapping and ties; raw corpus comparison not equivalent to engraver ground truth or performance; no independent test run here.
recommended_correction: Retain measured fix only for cases music21 demonstrably fails; expose source endpoints or UNKNOWN for ambiguous pairs and all snap decisions; test a few disputed bars against print. Consider simpler raw-list fallback if note-under coverage is not necessary for placement.
code_evidence: _slur_marks(); _pair() `best=max(...rank,k)`; EPS=1/100, SNAP=1/16; slurs() `_snap` and `ambiguous_no_winner`
claude_ruling: PARTLY. Ambiguous stops are counted (ambiguous_stops, ambiguous_no_winner: 7 stops in 6 files). Per-slur endpoints only if a consumer needs them. Spot-check disputed bars against print: LATER (plan).

reports: Pedal events (start, change, stop) with bars; pedalled spans; share of bars under pedal; sostenuto; una corda and tre corde from words.
definition: <direction-type><pedal type='start|stop|change|continue|sostenuto|resume|discontinue'>; words matched to a closed list for una corda / u.c. / tre corde / con pedale / senza pedale.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 expressions.PedalMark as the second reader. Our probe on 4 candidate files: music21 32 against 33 raw starts in one file, equal in the other three, so the raw count is the reference.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no finding. rung_pieces.py counts any object whose class name contains 'pedal' (replaced by this row).
pitfalls: 'Ped.' as words only; pedal lines with no stop; marks on staff 1 applying to the whole piano.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: Ped. at bar 1, change at bar 2, release at bar 3 -> 1 span with 1 change. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'con pedale' words with no marks -> 0 events, listed as text.
used_for: A.6 (first pedal), B.8 (connected pedal), 1.6 (pedalling), 7.4 (una corda), J.5 (pedal in tunes), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The structured pedal events are direct, but they can be associated with the whole piano part rather than staff 1; do not invent a hand or per-staff pedal when `<staff>` is omitted. Preserve `<pedal>` type, number, line/sign, start/change/stop and encoded depth if present, plus separate closed-vocabulary text. `una corda` is soft pedal, not sustain; these must not share a generic pedal label. An absent sign does not mean pedal is inappropriate.
implementation_observed: Custom XML pedal event extraction/pairer with shared MusicXML direction cursor, words vocabulary, printed marks, spans/changes/gaps and playback attrs; music21 provides layout.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Concrete music21 loss cases and 11,109-vs-11,063 start discrepancy justify raw pedal marks when accurately reporting printed pedal lines. But ~250 lines is much more than a simple detection flag and relies on custom time pairing.
correctness_and_musical_risks: `_pair` handles starts/sostenuto and stops, but `continue` and `resume` are accepted TYPES and counted without any state change; `discontinue` increments 'gaps' without closing/terminating pedal, so semantics can be misleading. `changes` are just counts, not precise timing. `bars_under_pedal` is union over staves and isn't audio pedal state; unknown-staff handling good. Shared direction cursor truncation risk.
test_quality_and_unverified: Dedicated test_e24 pins missing staff, overlap, changes, soft/sustain words, timed ordering and silent marks; real corpus has zero `continue/resume/discontinue`, thus their asserted handling cannot be validated by corpus runs.
recommended_correction: Define separate status for unsupported pedal continuation/resumption and discontinue (or implement MusicXML semantics), preserve event positions for changes and gaps, and mark `bars_under_pedal` as notated-line coverage only; prefer limited mark recognition if placement need is modest.
code_evidence: TYPES=(start,stop,change,continue,sostenuto,resume,discontinue); `_pair` processes stops/start/change/discontinue, silently ignores continue/resume
claude_ruling: AGREE. continue/resume are counted but do nothing to the span (0 in our files). LATER: report them as unsupported events, and say bars_under_pedal is notated-line coverage.

reports: Metronome marks (beat unit, dots, per minute, bar); <sound tempo> values (quarter notes per minute) with bars; the opening tempo word matched to a closed list (Grave to Prestissimo); a tempo map in quarter notes per minute.
definition: <metronome><beat-unit>, <beat-unit-dot>, <per-minute>; <sound tempo> is quarter notes per minute by the MusicXML definition. A dotted-quarter = 60 mark becomes 90 quarters per minute. A tempo word alone gives no number (a default number per word would be a guess).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 tempo.MetronomeMark.getQuarterBPM and metronomeMarkBoundaries as the second reader. partitura returned no tempo directions on a corpus file that has them, so it is not used.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated on named items (Op. 10 No. 1 quarter = 176; Asturias has no metronome mark but <sound tempo> 144).
pitfalls: A metronome mark and a <sound tempo> that disagree (report both); per-minute ranges ('100-108'); marks that are words only.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: quarter = 120 -> 120. Fail: no tempo at all -> UNKNOWN. Fool: dotted quarter = 60 in 6/8 -> 90 quarters per minute, not 60.
used_for: Notes per second (D01), step 4 generator check (exercise at the requested tempo)
why_easy: Direct read plus one unit conversion.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Keep three distinct observations: notated metronome mark, `<sound tempo>` playback value, and text tempo. Do not silently choose one if they disagree. Confirm MusicXML metronome ranges or metric-modulation equality are handled as nonnumeric/partial rather than parsed as a single BPM; use beat-unit dots for conversions and position before first note correctly. An opening mark after sounding notes is not opening tempo. Conditional durations in D01 must remain UNKNOWN when sound tempo looks like an exporter default.
implementation_observed: music21 MetronomeMark conversions and text; targeted raw read of overlapping <sound tempo>; segments qpm map with explicit provenance/conflicts and unknown opening span.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Good reuse of music21 tempo/metronome beat unit, justified raw patch for playback attribute lost on imported metronome. Correctly avoids music21's invented tempo words.
correctness_and_musical_risks: The key source-precedence choice (once any metronome appears, ignore later sound-only tempo) is a heuristic: later sound-only marks can be actual tempo changes; report them but D01 then computes rate using an obsolete metronome span. Numeric metronome in footnote/annotation can invent a tempo change, acknowledged in header. Attaching raw tempo by bar+offset across parts can merge unrelated directions; 1st mark is moved to zero if before first printed note even when physically later, which is okay only if no sounding notes before it. `directions` loses fractional raw offsets. Note that metric modulations are UNKNOWN rather than solved.
test_quality_and_unverified: Dedicated test_e25 covers dotted units, same-direction playback discrepancy, sound 120 default, after-notes opening, metric-modulation and conflict. No execution in this environment; disputed corpus output not independently checked.
recommended_correction: Keep notated tempo separate from playback map, with UNKNOWN where ambiguous; do not globally discard genuine later sound-only changes without a source-specific reason. Use exact fractional direction offsets and demonstrate rates on hand-checked score excerpt before trusting general difficulty.
code_evidence: tempo(): `has_metronome`; `use=notated if has_metronome else ...`; `sound_only_marks`; raw directions(root,'direction')
claude_ruling: AGREE this is a policy choice. Ruling: the PRINTED metronome mark is the tempo a learner reads, so it stays primary; playback-only changes after it are not silently lost: FIXED in D01, which now reports playback_only_tempo_marks_set_aside. The footnote metronome case (Op. 10/3) stays a known limit.

reports: Each rit., rall., accel., a tempo, Tempo I, rubato, allargando, stringendo, meno mosso, più mosso, and swing or straight-eighths directions (words, or the <swing> element), with bar; unrecognised direction words listed unclassified.
definition: <direction-type><words> matched case-insensitively to the closed list above and its abbreviations (rit., ritard., ritardando, rall., rallentando, accel., accelerando). Anything else is listed as 'other words', never classified.
implementation: Raw walk over <words>; music21 TextExpression as the second reader (music21 does not turn these into RitardandoSpanner from XML).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated on named items (Op. 9 No. 2 'poco rit.', 'a tempo'); French words ('Animez un peu') stayed unclassified.
pitfalls: Words in other languages; words split across two directions.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: 'rit.' at bar 15, 'a tempo' at bar 17 -> 2 entries. Fail: none -> empty. Fool: 'ritmico' (a character word) -> other words, not a ritardando.
in_our_files: words present in 553 of 842 (65.7%); tempo-change share not counted yet
used_for: A.6 (ritardando), 7.8 (tempo changes in reading), J.1 and 2.4 (a swing direction in a piece), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Closed word list; unknown words are listed, not guessed.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — The `reports` column promises rubato, allargando, stringendo, a tempo, Swing and straight-eighths, but the `definition` lists only rit/rall/accel variants. Make the closed vocabulary explicit and comprehensive for those promised kinds, plus parse structured `<swing>` independently. Simple substring matching must not classify `ritmico` or `accelerated` as rit/accel. Unrecognized words retain the raw text; they are not an absence of expression.
implementation_observed: music21 TextExpression and closed normalized vocabulary for rit/rall/stringendo etc, with raw structured <swing> due import gap; negations and joining fragments.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Appropriate library source for word text; bespoke vocabulary is a classification decision, not duplicating a mature semantic dictionary. Raw swing patch addresses a documented hole; nevertheless 256 lines for tempo words is high maintenance if all the app wants is general difficulty.
correctness_and_musical_risks: `other_words` includes negated vocabulary when `hits` is empty, so negated markers are redundantly listed as unclassified. At most two adjacent fragments merged only if neither recognized; can create spurious joins when unrelated word labels share bar+offset across staves because found keyed globally by text+position. Order of words is insertion order from music21, not necessarily document order after split. Counted broad corpus grammar is limited to its current languages; UNKNOWN preferable to forcing interpretation.
test_quality_and_unverified: Dedicated test_e26 reportedly covers negation, swing, joining, tempo I and boundary regexes; raw whole-corpus comparison has identical matcher vocabulary, not an independent musical ground truth.
recommended_correction: Keep closed vocabulary, preserve raw text and uncertainty; restrict fragment joins to same originating direction/staff where possible and label approximate. No need further complexity for broad difficulty.
code_evidence: VOCAB, classify(), tempo_change(): `by_pos`, join and `if not hits: other.setdefault`
claude_ruling: AGREE minor. NO CHANGE.

reports: Per staff: share of notes with a <fingering>, substitutions (e.g. 3-1), bars; digit-only <words> or lyrics listed separately as possible fingering.
definition: <notations><technical><fingering> (with substitution and alternate attributes).
implementation: Raw walk; music21 articulations.Fingering as the second reader. partitura keeps them on note.technical (its iter_all found none).
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (Hanon 1 right hand 61 digits; Mozart K. 2 easy had 0 <fingering> but 71 digit words).
pitfalls: Fingering typed as words or lyrics; '0'; stacked chord fingerings.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: five fingered notes -> share 5 of n. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: digits typed as lyrics -> 0 fingerings, listed as possible fingering text.
used_for: Information for lessons and Haiku agents (scale and early-position pieces: P.4, A.2, B.4, 1.2); step 4 generator check (fingering printed where the exercise promises it)
why_easy: Direct read.
chatgpt_independent_review: ACCEPT WITH EDGE TEST — Structured fingering is a reliable printed fact. Count per note and per chord rather than one digit per sounding note; distinguish substitutions and alternates. Preserve digit-only free text as an unverified possible fingering, not a match. Use for showing/choosing teaching material only: a printed finger 3 does not prove the fingering suits the learner or is actually played.
implementation_observed: music21 Fingering exact class on printed notes and chords; parses digits/pairs/stacked strings; reports substitutions, alternatives and ambiguous other text.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Strong direct music21 reuse, avoids copying raw technical-tag parser; custom compact textual disambiguation is sensible and scope-limited.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Header correctly notes chord-member fingering association lost during import and counts marks rather than per-note correctness; `possible_text` digit-only words/lyrics are not proof of fingering. `_STACK` accepts dangling separators, creating odd pseudo-multiple digits; _POSSIBLE may mishandle punctuation. Printed fingering attached to hidden chord member may be counted (known caveat). No tempo/difficulty inference.
test_quality_and_unverified: test_e27 includes finger 0/6, pluck-subclass confusion, stacked/substitution text, chord-member unknown and free digit text; header describes importer corpus checks not independently run.
recommended_correction: Keep music21; expose unknown member pairing and do not assign technique requirements from printed finger numbers; tighten malformed stacked-text handling only where real files show problem.
code_evidence: fingering(): `type(a) is m.articulations.Fingering`; `_form`/`_STACK`; `possible_text`
claude_ruling: AGREE. NO CHANGE.

chatgpt_ids: notation.chord-symbols; harmony.rhythm and harmony.chord-vocabulary (from symbols only)

definition: <harmony> with <root>/<root-step>, <root-alter>, <kind>, <bass>; chord names typed as <words> are not counted here.
implementation: Raw walk; music21 harmony.ChordSymbol as the second reader for <harmony> elements only.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: own reader and music21's <harmony> reader equal on 459 of 460 items; duplicates on two staves were common (4,984 down to 3,619 after removing them). music21's text parser misread 'Bb7' as root B, so text chord names are left out.
pitfalls: Duplicates on both staves; guitar-frame symbols; Roman-numeral or function kinds.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: C, F, G7 over three bars -> 3 symbols, 3 distinct. Fail: none -> 0. Fool: 'Bb7' typed as words -> 0 symbols here.
used_for: B.7 (first lead sheet: a piece with chord symbols), 4.3, 5.3, J.1, J.3, PR.1 (lead sheets), step 4 generator check
why_easy: Direct read; the library agreed on 459 of 460.
chatgpt_independent_review: REVISE — Read `<harmony>` structurally; preserve root alteration, bass inversion, chord-kind modifiers and unknown kinds instead of lumping everything into major/minor/7/other where the lessons need extensions. Deduplicate only truly duplicate annotations at the same musical position and with identical content; two different chords at the same position could be conflicting evidence, not safe to merge. N.C. often has no root; do not drop it as a parser error. Separate label recognition from meaningful progression/harmonic analysis.
implementation_observed: music21 ChordSymbol/NoChord, root/kind/bass/degree/functional labels; dedups same-position same-content copies and reports conflicting simultaneous symbols.
implementation_and_library_reuse: Strong reuse of library harmony parse and chord-kind aliases; custom grouping/class distinctions justified by actual importer pitfalls, particularly `kind none` vs NoChord.
correctness_and_musical_risks: Deduplicates truly separate symbols in distinct parts if same location/content, which can remove repeated lead-sheet labels intentionally per part; sources retained but semantics not always same. Uses generated harmony figure for display: library may normalize differently from printed text; preserve text + chordKind. Some invalid/rootless harmony can fail entire music21 parse BEFORE this function, acknowledged. `_name(cs.root())` assumes pitch exists if cs.pitches nonempty. Not sounding harmony.
test_quality_and_unverified: test_e29 is comprehensive on staff-copy, chords, extensions, empty kinds, no-chord, function labels and conflicts; tests are handwritten, actual corpus symbol use low (39/842) per comment.
recommended_correction: Keep library route; distinguish duplicate importer staff copies from intentional duplication across independent parts, and never equate chord symbol with realized notes.
code_evidence: _read(); chord_symbols(): key=(bi,off,content) excludes part; `sources` and `duplicates_detail`
claude_ruling: PARTLY. Merging same symbol at the same place across parts is right for piano scores (staff copies); the 7 genuine conflicts in 2 files are kept. NO CHANGE.

reports: Slash noteheads and slash measure styles, bars.
definition: <notehead>slash</notehead>; <measure-style><slash> or <beat-repeat>.
implementation: Raw walk.
library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: validated (So Danço Samba 28 slashes; no measure-style slash anywhere).
pitfalls: None known beyond rarity.
tests_pass_fail_fool: Pass: four slash noteheads in a bar -> 4. Fail: normal noteheads -> 0. Fool: x noteheads -> 0.
used_for: Comping charts (B.7, J and PR rungs); very rare in our files
why_easy: Direct read; low value.

fact: Span of notes struck together, per staff

fact: Melodic leaps and jumps, per staff

library_and_prior_evidence: Old branch: no measured finding (the app detector counted steps, skips and leaps on chord tops and bottoms). music21 melodicIntervals and its jSymbolic interval features mix both staves, so per-staff is our own.

Measure interval direction, written generic size and elapsed time; jump >12 semitones within 2 beats is an operational statistic, not a universal definition of difficulty or a real position shift.

Outer edge ignores voice roles. Not proof of grade.

recommended_correction: Keep as measured displacement and written-voice interval; don't treat the fixed jump flag as hard difficulty or reach threshold; optional corroboration via hand directions.

claude_ruling: AGREE. NO CHANGE (limits are in the comment).
